description:
RawDrive Live Camera Sync

1. Executive Summary
RawDrive Live Camera Sync enables wedding photographers to automatically upload photos from tethered cameras or SD card folders directly to client galleries with zero manual intervention. Photos appear in the cloud gallery within seconds of capture, allowing real‑time client collaboration during live events.

Primary Value: Transform 3‑day delivery → same‑day proofs during wedding receptions.

2. Business Objectives
Objective	Metric	Target
Eliminate manual imports	Hours saved per wedding	8 hours
Enable live client collaboration	Galleries updated during events	100%
Drive Studio plan adoption	Monthly recurring revenue	$149 × 2K studios
Increase photographer retention	Churn reduction	25%
Support peak wedding season	Concurrent syncing photographers	50K
3. User Personas & Primary Use Cases
Primary Persona: Wedding Photographer (Live Events)
text
Rohan, 32, shoots 15 weddings/month
Pain: "Clients wait 3 days for proofs → lost upsell opportunities"
Goal: "Show ceremony photos during reception → immediate album orders"
Use Case 1: Tethered Live Shooting
text
1. Connect Canon R5 to laptop before ceremony
2. Map camera folder → "Ananya Wedding" gallery
3. Shoot 300 ceremony photos → client proofs on phone during reception
4. Client favorites 47 photos → immediate album discussion
Use Case 2: SD Card Hot‑Swap
text
1. Map SD card slot D:\DCIM → "Rohan Engagement" gallery
2. Insert card 1 (200 photos) → auto‑upload during portraits
3. Swap card 2 during reception → seamless continuation
4. End of night: 847 photos live, client actively proofing
Use Case 3: Multi‑Shooter Team
text
✅ Shooter 1: Tethered camera → ceremony sub‑gallery
✅ Shooter 2: SD cards → portrait sub‑gallery  
✅ Both streams → single client‑viewable gallery
4. Functional Requirements
4.1 Folder/Gallery Mapping
text
R1.1: Photographers map local folders to RawDrive galleries (1:1)
R1.2: Support sub‑folder → sub‑gallery mapping
R1.3: Multiple folders → single gallery (team shooting)
R1.4: Visual confirmation: "C:\Weddings\Ananya ↔ Ananya Wedding Live"
4.2 Real‑Time Synchronization
text
R2.1: Detect folder changes <2 seconds (add/delete/rename/move)
R2.2: New photos auto‑upload to mapped gallery
R2.3: Deletions propagate cloud → local (optional)
R2.4: Renames sync both directions
R2.5: Live status: "247/1,234 photos synced 🔄"
4.6 Camera Tethering Support
text
R4.6.1: Auto‑detect tethered cameras (Canon/Nikon/Sony)
R4.6.2: USB/WiFi/Ethernet connections
R4.6.3: Live view monitoring (DCIM folders)
R4.6.4: Battery/storage status display
4.7 Business Intelligence
text
R4.7.1: Sync dashboard (web + desktop)
R4.7.2: Monthly stats: GB synced, photos processed
R4.7.3: Per‑gallery sync status badges
5. Non‑Functional Requirements
5.1 Performance
text
NF1.1: 50K photographers syncing simultaneously
NF1.2: Photo capture → cloud gallery <10 seconds
NF1.3: 99.99% sync success rate
NF1.4: Desktop app <100MB RAM idle
5.2 Availability
text
NF2.1: Offline operation (queue changes locally)
NF2.2: Auto‑resume on reconnect
NF2.3: Conflict resolution (local wins default)
5.3 Platforms
text
NF3.1: Windows 10/11, macOS 13+, Ubuntu 22.04+
NF3.2: Camera support: Canon/Nikon/Sony (top 80% market)
6. Microservice Architecture (High‑Level)
text
Desktop App (Tauri)
  ↓ Real‑time folder changes
Sync Agent Microservice (KEDA autoscaling)
  ↓ Events to specialized services
├── Upload Microservice (new photos)
├── Gallery Microservice (deletions/metadata)
└── Redis (live status dashboard)
Autoscaling: KEDA scales Sync Agent based on sync event volume (5→40 pods).

7. Monetization & Business Model
text
FREE: Manual sync, 5GB/month, 2 folders
PRO ($49/mo): Auto‑sync, 500GB/month, 10 folders
STUDIO ($149/mo): Unlimited + camera tethering + team sync
Expected Revenue: $298K ARR (2K Studio subscribers)

8. Success Metrics & KPIs
Metric	Target	Business Impact
Sync success rate	99.99%	Trust
Capture → cloud latency	<10s	Live collaboration
Studio plan conversion	25% Pro → Studio	$100/mo uplift
Churn reduction	25%	Retention
Photos synced/month	10M	Scale

# RawDrive Live Camera Sync - Comprehensive Specification

## 1. Problem Statement

Wedding photographers currently spend 8+ hours manually importing, organizing, and uploading photos from their cameras to client galleries after events. This delay prevents real-time client collaboration during live events (e.g., showing ceremony photos during receptions) and misses upsell opportunities. RawDrive Live Camera Sync eliminates this friction by automatically detecting new photos in watched folders and syncing them to cloud galleries within seconds of capture.

## 2. User Story

**As a** wedding photographer shooting live events,  
**I want** automatic synchronization between my camera's output folder and my client's cloud gallery,  
**So that** clients can view, favorite, and discuss photos in real-time during the event without any manual intervention.

## 3. Acceptance Criteria

### Happy Path Scenarios

**Scenario 1: Initial Folder-Gallery Mapping**
- **GIVEN** a photographer is authenticated with a valid workspace
- **WHEN** they map a local folder path to an existing gallery
- **THEN** the system creates a sync mapping record, validates the folder exists, and displays "C:\Photos\Wedding ↔ Ananya Wedding Live" confirmation

**Scenario 2: Real-Time Photo Detection & Upload**
- **GIVEN** a folder is actively mapped to a gallery with sync enabled
- **WHEN** a new photo (JPEG/RAW) is saved to the watched folder
- **THEN** the system detects the change within 2 seconds, queues the upload, and completes cloud sync within 10 seconds (for files <50MB on stable connection)

**Scenario 3: Multi-Folder Team Shooting**
- **GIVEN** two photographers have separate folders mapped to the same gallery
- **WHEN** both photographers save photos simultaneously
- **THEN** both photo streams merge into the single gallery with correct timestamps and photographer attribution

**Scenario 4: Live Status Dashboard**
- **GIVEN** an active sync session is running
- **WHEN** the photographer checks the sync status
- **THEN** they see real-time progress: "247/1,234 photos synced 🔄", upload speed, and ETA

### Edge Case Scenarios

**Scenario 5: Offline Operation & Resume**
- **GIVEN** the network connection is lost during sync
- **WHEN** the connection is restored
- **THEN** the system automatically resumes uploading from where it stopped with no duplicate uploads

**Scenario 6: Rapid File Changes (Burst Mode)**
- **GIVEN** a photographer shoots 10+ photos per second in burst mode
- **WHEN** files are written rapidly to the watched folder
- **THEN** the system batches file detection efficiently without missing any files or overwhelming the upload queue

**Scenario 7: File Rename/Move Within Folder**
- **GIVEN** a photo exists in the watched folder and has been synced
- **WHEN** the photographer renames or moves the file within the folder structure
- **THEN** the system updates the cloud asset metadata without re-uploading the file content

**Scenario 8: Duplicate Detection**
- **GIVEN** a photo has already been synced to the gallery
- **WHEN** the same file (by SHA256 hash) is added again
- **THEN** the system skips the duplicate upload and logs the detection

### Error Handling Scenarios

**Scenario 9: Invalid Folder Path**
- **GIVEN** a photographer attempts to map a non-existent folder
- **WHEN** the mapping request is submitted
- **THEN** the system returns error: "Folder path does not exist: {path}" and does not create the mapping

**Scenario 10: Insufficient Storage**
- **GIVEN** the workspace has reached its storage quota
- **WHEN** new photos are detected in the watched folder
- **THEN** the system pauses sync, notifies the user "Storage quota exceeded", and queues files for retry when space is available

**Scenario 11: Corrupted/Incomplete File**
- **GIVEN** a file is being written to the watched folder (incomplete)
- **WHEN** the system detects the new file
- **THEN** the system waits for file stability (no changes for 2 seconds) before initiating upload

## 4. Technical Context

| Aspect | Value |
|--------|-------|
| **Affected Services** | New: `sync-service` microservice; Modified: `gallery-service`, `upload-service`, `backend` |
| **Frontend Changes** | New: `SyncDashboard` page, `useFolderSync` hook, `SyncStatusWidget` component |
| **Database** | New tables: `sync_mappings`, `sync_sessions`, `sync_events` |
| **Dependencies** | Backend: `watchdog` (file watching), `aiofiles`; Frontend: File System Access API |
| **Constraints** | Browser-based folder watching limited to File System Access API (Chrome/Edge); Full tethering requires desktop app (future phase) |
| **Patterns to Follow** | WebSocket from gallery-service, TUS upload from upload-service, useUpload queue pattern |
| **Rate Limits** | 50 req/min sync status updates, 200 file events/min per session |
| **Storage** | Uses existing R2/BYOS infrastructure |

## 5. Non-Goals (Explicitly Out of Scope)

1. **Native Desktop App (Tauri/Electron)** - Phase 1 uses browser File System Access API; native app is future phase
2. **Camera Tethering Protocol (PTP/MTP)** - Not implementing direct USB camera communication; photographers use camera software's output folder
3. **Cloud-to-Local Sync (Bidirectional Delete)** - Only local→cloud sync; deletions do NOT propagate
4. **RAW File Processing/Conversion** - Files sync as-is; processing handled by existing pipeline
5. **Multi-Device Sync** - Single browser session per mapping; no cross-device folder sync
6. **Video File Support** - Focus on still images only (JPEG, RAW formats)
7. **Free Tier** - Feature requires PRO ($49/mo) or STUDIO ($149/mo) subscription

## 6. Implementation Tasks

## 7. Success Metrics

| Metric | Target | Measurement Method |
|--------|--------|-------------------|

| Sync success rate | 99.9% | `sync_events_succeeded / sync_events_total` |
| Concurrent sync sessions | 1,000+ per instance | Load test with KEDA scaling |
| WebSocket connection stability | < 0.1% disconnect rate | `sync_ws_disconnects_total / sync_ws_connections_total` |
| Memory footprint (frontend) | < 50MB additional | Chrome DevTools memory profiler |
| PRO/STUDIO conversion | 25% of photographers with >5 syncs | Analytics funnel tracking |

## 8. Risks & Mitigations

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|------------|--------|------------|
| File System Access API browser support limited (Chrome/Edge only) | High | Medium | Clear browser requirements in UI; roadmap native desktop app for Phase 2 |
| Rapid burst mode overwhelms upload queue | Medium | High | Implement adaptive batching (debounce 500ms), queue depth limits (100 files), and backpressure signaling |
| Large RAW files (100MB+) cause timeout | Medium | Medium | Increase TUS chunk size to 10MB, implement parallel chunk uploads, extend timeout to 5 minutes |
| Network instability during sync | High | Medium | Implement robust retry with exponential backoff, local queue persistence in IndexedDB |
| Storage quota exceeded mid-sync | Low | High | Pre-flight quota check, graceful pause with user notification, queue files for retry |
| WebSocket connection limits per gallery | Medium | Low | Implement connection pooling, limit to 100 connections per sync session |
| Cross-instance sync state inconsistency | Low | High | Use Redis as source of truth for session state, implement event sourcing pattern |
